channel.title: Antony Clements — Notes on AI-augmented software engineering
channel.description: Essays and notes by Antony Clements on AI-augmented software engineering.

item.title: Experiments: finding where project memory helps
item.description: Testing where persistent project memory helps agents, where it adds work, and what the evidence means for Augmented Workflow.

item.title: Picking up where the last agent stopped
item.description: The next session should not have to reconstruct a conversation we could have summarised properly before leaving.

item.title: Teaching the repo what you keep correcting
item.description: The aim is for the next session to benefit from attention already spent, while leaving room to discover that the old advice no longer fits.

item.title: Did you wash your hands?
item.description: Deterministic checks in agentic development. The missing records, stale reviews and broken links are questions a script can answer. That leaves me more attention for the things it can’t.

item.title: Code Without a Theory
item.description: AI agents produce code without building Naur's theory — and the review process built for human-scale code can't keep up. On the flipped cost of writing versus reviewing, the review ratchet, and what actually holds up.
